issues.detail: The Hebrew 'בַּת עֵינֵךְ' means 'the daughter of your eye' (i.e., your eye/pupil), not '你眼中的女兒' (the daughter in your eye). The Chinese rendering '你眼中的女兒' could be misread as a literal daughter, whereas the Hebrew idiom refers to the eye itself. This changes the meaning of the final clause.
